WPMS/2362/2026
Sri Kartikey Garg --Petitioner
 Versus
State Bank Of India --Respondent
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J
1. Mr. Piyush Garg, learned counsel for
the petitioner.
2. Mr. Ravi Sehgal, learned counsel for
the respondent is connected virtually.
3. Petitioner has challenged the order
dated 28.04.2026 passed by Debts
Recovery Appellate Tribunal, Allahabad in
Dy. No. 1777 of 2024, whereby he was
asked to deposit minimum 25 percent of
the amount due, as a condition for
entertaining his appeal under Section 18
of The Securitisation and Reconstruction
of Financial Assets and Enforcement of
Security Interest Act, 2002 (in short
'SARFAESI Act'). It is further provided in
the said order that if petitioner does not
deposit the said amount, before the next
date fixed, his appeal shall be treated to
have been dismissed.
4. Petitioner contends that he is
neither the borrower nor the guarantor in
respect of any loan from State Bank of
India, therefore, the condition of pre-deposit of minimum 25 percent of the
amount of debt would not apply to him.
It is contended that first proviso to
Section 18(1) of SARFAESI Act makes a
distinction between a borrower and a
person other than borrower; as regards
borrower, second proviso to Section

UKHC010137142026
2026:UHC:7709
18(1) provides that his appeal shall not
be entertained unless he deposits with
the Appellate Tribunal 50 percent of the
amount of debt due from him, which can
be reduced from 50 percent to 25
percent by third proviso to Section 18(1),
however, for persons other than
borrower, there is no mandatory
condition regarding pre-deposit of any
amount for filing appeal.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner
further submits that by the impugned
order, it is provided that in case
petitioner fails to deposit minimum 25
percent of the amount due, then his
appeal shall be treated to have been
dismissed. It is thus contended that since
the scheme of Section 18(1) of
SARFAESI Act was not considered in its
entirety by learned Appellate Tribunal,
therefore, the order impugned deserves
to be set-aside.
6. This Court finds some substance in
the contention raised on behalf of the
petitioner. First proviso to Section 18(1)
of the SARFAESI Act provides that fee for
filing appeal may be different for a
borrower and person other than the
borrower. Second proviso to Section
18(1) mandates that borrower will be
required to deposit 50 percent of the
amount of debt due from him, as claimed
by Secured Creditors or determined by
the Debts Recovery Tribunal, whichever
is less. Third proviso to Section 18(1),
however, enables the Appellate Tribunal
to reduce the amount of pre-deposit, in
case of a borrower, from 50 percent to
25 percent. However, it is silent about
person other than borrower. There is no
provision in Section 18(1), dealing with

UKHC010137142026
2026:UHC:7709
the amount which persons other than the
borrower are required to deposit as a
condition for maintaining the appeal.
7. Learned Appellate Tribunal has
relied upon third proviso to Section 18(1)
of the SARFAESI Act for holding that the
amount cannot be reduced below 25
percent of debt due. Since petitioner
contends that he is neither borrower nor
guarantor, therefore, whether third
proviso would be attracted to the appeal,
filed by petitioner, is a debatable issue,
although on a plain reading, third proviso
does not appear to be attracted in case
of other person.
8. Since this aspect has not been dealt
with in the impugned order dated
28.04.2026, therefore, the same is set-aside. Accordingly, the writ petition is
allowed. The matter is remitted back to
learned Debts Recovery Appellate
Tribunal to decide the question whether
the condition regarding pre-deposit of
certain amount of debt due, as contained
in third proviso to Section 18(1) would
be attracted to a person, who is neither
borrower nor guarantor.
 (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J)
